Palestinian director Ahmed Hassouna’s film is one of several at the Venice Film Festival in 2026 about journalism, whether the high stakes faced by war correspondents, or the morally ambiguous methods used by certain media to gain viewers. questions.title: Who will win Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election?
questions.background: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, where the presence of US military bases is a major political issue.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results announced by Okinawa's election authorities, either directly or as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution : The question resolves when the winner of Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Edging challenger Genta Koja into a narrow favorite (0.49 -> 0.53) ahead of two-term incumbent Denny Tamaki (0.50 -> 0.46; 0.01 left across four minor candidates) after early-campaign polling and organizational data published Aug 30-Sep 1. A joint Ryukyu Shimpo / JX Press internet survey conducted Aug 28-30 (published Sep 1) found Koja and Tamaki dead even ('横一線') with 50% undecided and 70% intending to vote—a warning sign for an All-Okinawa incumbent who led comfortably throughout 2022. Separately, an Okinawa Times survey of all 41 municipal mayors (Aug 30) showed 29 (~71%) endorsing six-party-backed Koja versus only 6 for Tamaki (down from 7 in 2022) and 6 neutral/unanswered, reflecting local dissatisfaction over Okinawa budget cuts. Additionally, a leaked LDP 4th internal survey reported by former Sankei journalist Gentaro Saegusa (Aug 31) claimed Koja overtook Tamaki 44.1% to 40.9% following Mikio Shimoji's non-filing (reversing Tamaki's +4.4 mid-August lead in the same tracking series). We explicitly discount the unverified partisan leak—major papers have not corroborated it, JAG Japan reportedly still shows Tamaki slightly ahead, internet polls can lean slightly younger/more conservative than Okinawa RDD phone polls, and 50% remain undecided—keeping the race a near coin-flip (53-46) pending weekend RDD phone polls.

questions.title: Which country will Washington propose as a possible venue for renewed trilateral Russia–Ukraine ceasefire talks by September 25, 2026?
questions.background: The United States has been involved in efforts to broker an end to the Russia–Ukraine war.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country publicly identified by Ukraine's president as Washington's proposed location for renewed talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, using the proposal current as of September 25, 2026. A suggested location is sufficient; the talks need not have taken place. Resolution Date : 2026-09-25 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No trilateral talks venue has been publicly named by Zelenskyy as of Sep 1: Zelenskyy held a 'detailed and constructive' call on Aug 31 with Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to lock in dates for their visit to Ukraine while they prepare Russian contacts, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated on Sep 1 there are 'no specifics yet.' However, Aug 29-Sep 1 diplomacy shifts venue weights: United States rises (+0.04 to 0.23) after Axios reported (Aug 30) that CIA Director John Ratcliffe proposed a Trump-Putin-Zelensky summit in Moscow, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent hosted Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov on US soil in North Carolina (Aug 31) to discuss Trump's peace plan, and late-September UNGA in New York nears the Sep 25 deadline. Meanwhile, Turkey is trimmed (-0.03 to 0.25) because Ankara summoned Ukraine's ambassador on Aug 29 over Ukrainian attacks on two Turkish ships in the Black Sea, and the Aug 31-Sep 1 SCO Bishkek summit closed without any Putin-Erdogan Ukraine mediation initiative. Switzerland (0.21, Feb 2026 Geneva host) holds steady while Gulf hosts UAE (-0.01 to 0.10) and Saudi Arabia (0.07) remain dampened by ongoing US-Iran conflict tensions highlighted in the Sep 1 SCO Bishkek Declaration (0.14 remains outside the top 5).

questions.title: Who will receive the longest prison sentence at the trial over the July 2023 burglary of Gianluigi Donnarumma's Paris home?
questions.background: Goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his partner were attacked during a burglary at their Paris home in July 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Paris Criminal Court's judgment, as documented by the court or reliable contemporaneous reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the defendant receiving the longest total prison sentence in the trial verdict delivered by September 30, 2026. Compare sentences actually imposed, including any suspended portions, rather than sentences requested by prosecutors. Later appeals do not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The defendant's name as publicly reported.
questions.current_reasoning: July 11, 2026 AFP/Le Parisien/L'Equipe reporting officially confirmed the Paris Criminal Court (tribunal correctionnel) trial of the three adult defendants for September 10-11, 2026, eliminating postponement risk past Sept 30. The two minor suspects were already tried separately in juvenile court in early July (receiving 4 and 3 years, including 1 year suspended), so they are definitively excluded. The July 11 indictment details further strengthen Ilyas Kherbouch's ('Ganito', 21) position as clear favorite for the longest sentence: beyond his principal-mastermind designation, 7-year prior for the Simone Zanoni home-jacking, and March 2026 Villepinte prison escape, investigators attributed direct SMS instructions on the eve and night of the burglary to his line and found photos of the bloodied, sequestered third adult defendant on Kherbouch's phone. Co-mastermind Khyan M. ('Kiki', 21) remains reported solely with an initialed surname (0.10, with 0.12 left for Khyan M.'s full surname if published at trial, a tie, or the third defendant).

questions.title: Which stadium will UEFA select to host the 2029 men's Champions League final?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UEFA's official announcement awarding hosting rights for the 2029 men's Champions League final, or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution Date : Resolve when UEFA publicly announces its venue selection. Subsequent venue changes will not alter the answer. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the selected stadium.
questions.current_reasoning: Upgrading Camp Nou (0.56 -> 0.65) over Wembley Stadium (0.44 -> 0.35) in this confirmed two-stadium race decided by the UEFA Executive Committee on Sep 14-15, 2026. An Aug 27 Football Ground Guide report explicitly states that the revamped ~105,000-seat Camp Nou is now considered the 'clear favourite' for the 2029 Champions League final following a major UEFA shift and improving relations between Joan Laporta and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin. Furthermore, local Aug 2026 match listings confirm Barcelona are already actively hosting La Liga games back at Camp Nou (vs Athletic Club on Aug 27), easing renovation-delay concerns, while Wembley already hosted the 2024 UCL final and hosts the Euro 2028 final less than a year earlier. We cap Camp Nou at 0.65 ahead of the formal committee vote because Madrid's Metropolitano hosts the 2027 UCL final and Wembley remains a strong fallback.

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country had publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons as of Aug 25, 2026. However, Aug 14 reporting (Asia Times / The War Zone) revealed a notable US doctrinal shift: US SPACECOM Commander Gen. Stephen Whiting announced offensive kinetic and non-kinetic ASAT capabilities ('integrated space fires' and counter-pLEO) as a top military priority, with US defense officials explicitly stressing the joint force must possess a 'credible, acknowledged ability' to attack adversary space assets (while noting the ground-based CCS jammer remains the only publicly acknowledged US offensive ASAT to date). Meanwhile, Aug 8 reporting on Golden Dome confirmed $3.2B for space-based interceptor prototypes targeting late-2026 tests and 2027 flight demos (future, not yet deployed). With Pentagon leadership openly building the case for public acknowledgment ahead of the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference, US probability rises from 0.42 to 0.49 while Russia (0.25, active co-orbital ASAT testing), China (0.12), France (0.08), and India (0.03) remain key alternatives.
